successors.name: Teutonic Order
successors.text: the Prussian tribal lands, taken by the Teutonic Order in the Prussian Crusade, 1230-1283: 'the conquest of the Prussians ended' in 1283

ledger.x: 997: the first dated event on Prussian land: Adalbert of Prague slain among the Prussians.
1233: the Order founds Marienwerder in Pomesania.
1236: the fighting for Pomesania ends with the submission.
1238: the Order's campaigns against the Bartians, Natangians and Warmians begin.
1253: Warmia, Natangia, Bartia and Pogesania pass to the Order.
1253: the fighting of the first uprising ends.
20 September 1260: the Great Prussian Uprising begins after Durbe.
20 September 1260: the risings retake the countryside.
1277: the rising is over; the central tribes have submitted.
1277: the lands the risings had retaken pass back to the Order.
1283: Nadruvia and Skalvia pass to the Order.
1283: the conquest of the Prussians ends.

wars.name: Prussian Crusade
wars.outcome: Teutonic Order victory: the Prussian tribes were conquered between 1233 and 1283; the Order held Prussia by the end of the 13th century.

wars.name: First Prussian Uprising
wars.outcome: The Order kept the land: the Prussians beat it at Rensen (1244) and Krücken (November 1249) but lacked siege capability; Swantopelk of Pomerelia stopped aiding them in 1248; the Treaty of Christburg was signed in February 1249.

wars.name: Great Prussian Uprising
wars.outcome: The Order recovered the land: Heilsberg fell in 1274; the central tribes had submitted by 1277; many free peasants became serfs.

certainty.note: Tribal lands without a common state: the page's map boundaries are approximate and the Sudovian and Skalvian edges are the least certain.
